abstract: CESifo randomized controlled trial measuring the impact of generative AI tools on retail sales productivity, finding total factor productivity (TFP) gains ranging from 0% to 16.3% depending on the specific application and worker characteristics. The wide range of effects highlights that AI's productivity impact is highly context-dependent, with some implementations yielding substantial gains while others show no measurable improvement.
keyFindings: Generative AI produces 0-16.3% sales TFP gains in retail settings
Productivity gains are highly variable across workers and implementation contexts
Some AI implementations show no measurable productivity improvement
Worker characteristics and task fit are key determinants of AI productivity effects
methodology: CESifo randomized controlled trial in retail settings, randomizing access to generative AI tools and measuring changes in sales-based total factor productivity across treatment and control groups.
qualifiers: Retail-specific results may not generalize to other sectors. The wide range (0-16.3%) reflects genuine heterogeneity rather than measurement imprecision. Short-term RCT may not capture learning effects that emerge over longer periods of AI tool use.
